newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 opens higher, buoyed by oil sector.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 opens higher, buoyed by oil sector.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index opened higher on Monday, led by buoyant oil stocks after the U.N. put the Iraq oil-for-food deal on hold, but dealers said gains were likely to be capped as U.S markets stayed shut for the Labor Day holiday.
By 0754 GMT the FTSE 100 was up 10.6 points at 3,878.2. Gainers were outweighing losers by roughly two-to-one.
"We're being left to our own devises today," said one dealer, referring to the U.S. holiday. "And there's no reason domestically to be selling this market," he added.
UK gilts edged slightly lower on weaker Bunds and were awaiting August PMI and MO data expected at 0830 GMT.
